statement: The regression loss, specifically the within-sample mean squared error (MSE) of a predictor for a sample of n data points with observed values Y and predicted values hat{Y}, is defined as MSE = (1/n) * sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - hat{Y}_i)^2 = (1/n) * e^T e, where e_i = Y_i - hat{Y}_i and e is the n x 1 error column vector. The supplied sources define this object directly and genuinely contain nothing to derive for the regression loss itself.

symbols.meaning: number of data points in the sample
vector of observed values of the variable being predicted
observed value for the i-th observation
predicted value for the i-th observation
prediction error (residual) Y_i - hat{Y}_i for observation i
number of out-of-sample data points used for cross-validation

properties.property: MSE is always a positive value that decreases as the error approaches zero.
properties.why: It is derived from the square of Euclidean distance.

properties.property: Within-sample MSE can be written in matrix notation as (1/n) * e^T e.
properties.why: The sum of squared scalar errors equals the inner product of the error column vector with itself.

properties.property: MSE can be computed on q out-of-sample data points as test MSE: (1/q) * sum_{i=n+1}^{n+q} (Y_i - hat{Y}_i)^2.
properties.why: Cross-validation evaluates the predictor on held-back or newly obtained data.

properties.property: In gradient descent algorithms, a factor of 1/2 is commonly introduced to the MSE.
properties.why: It provides ease of computation after taking the derivative.

properties.property: MSE is a consistent estimator of the error variance, given predictor consistency, but is not an unbiased estimator.
properties.why: The denominator used is sample size n rather than degrees of freedom (n - p or n - p - 1).

properties.property: In machine learning empirical risk minimization, MSE functions as the empirical risk estimating true risk.
properties.why: It measures average loss on an observed dataset as an estimate of average loss on the population distribution.

assumptions.assumption: Sample size n is a strictly positive integer (n >= 1).
assumptions.breaks_when: The dataset is empty (n = 0), causing division by zero.

assumptions.assumption: Observed values Y_i and predicted values hat{Y}_i are real-valued numerical quantities.
assumptions.breaks_when: Data points contain missing, non-numeric, or infinite values.

failure_modes.signature: MSE systematically underestimates error variance in small samples.
failure_modes.cause: Dividing the sum of squared errors by n instead of degrees of freedom (n - p or n - p - 1).

failure_modes.signature: MSE remains strictly positive even for the best fitted model.
failure_modes.cause: Inherent randomness in the data or missing information that the model does not account for.

shape: expected a derivation, produced a definition
